label: Diagram 1.11
caption: Diagram 1.11 | Key dimensions for handrails for common stairs in blocks of flats For buildings other than dwellings
description: The drawing is a side elevation of a straight flight of stairs rising left to right, with a handrail running parallel above the treads and short horizontal ends. A dashed diagonal line shows the slope of the stair, and vertical dashed lines mark the dimensions. Top left reads 'See paras 1.34–1.35'; the green band at the bottom reads 'Diagram 1.11 Key dimensions for handrails for common stairs in blocks of flats'. At the left, a vertical dimension of 1000mm runs from the lower reference line to the level of the left end of the handrail; a dimension marked 300mm min. is shown there with a vertical arrow to the rail and a horizontal double‑headed arrow between the rail's end and the first step. In the middle, a vertical dimension of 900mm runs from the dashed slope line up to the top of the handrail. On the right, a horizontal dimension of 300mm min. runs between the top step and the right end of the handrail, and a vertical dimension of 1000mm runs from the level of the top step to the top of the right end of the handrail.
